reading.body:
Resemble AI builds detection systems for AI-generated audio, video, and images, positioning itself in the trust and verification layer of synthetic media rather than creation tools.

The company's market exists because voice cloning and deepfake video calls have become fraud vectors at scale. FBI data cited in the context around this company places business email compromise losses involving AI voice at over three billion dollars in 2025, a two hundred fifty million dollar increase year over year. Detection of synthetic media is not a peripheral concern but a response to specific, quantified harm in enterprise operations.

Resemble AI's architecture choice, a world model designed to recognize physical impossibilities rather than pattern-matching alone, reflects a technical bet that detection requires reasoning about what the real world permits. The company offers deployment flexibility, on-premises or cloud, which matters for customers with data sensitivity around the media they need analyzed. Neither product launch velocity, customer count, nor financial performance is covered in this data, leaving the question of detection accuracy and adoption rate unresolved.

profile_text.body:
Resemble AI was founded in 2018 and is headquartered in Toronto. Its website describes the company as powering real-time deepfake detection for enterprise, with deployment on-prem or cloud and built to scale. The site says the company detects AI-generated audio, video, and images in real time with explainable results, using a system called DETECT-World that combines pattern matching and training with a world model architecture to recognize deviations from physical reality. The company describes itself as shaping responsible AI and bridging AI creation tools with trust. It won the T Challenge competition of T-Mobile US and Deutsche Telekom in 2025.

The product note for Resemble AI flags voice cloning and likeness/consent risk. No lawsuits or MCP servers are listed for the company. The site also reproduces third-party reports on deepfake-related fraud, including FBI data cited by Forbes that business email compromise scams stole over $3 billion in 2025, a $250 million increase attributed to AI voice cloning and deepfake video calls.
